program_overview.title: MySQL and SQL for Teens
program_overview.tagline: Every app a teenager uses is a database wearing a nice shirt. Five months from first query to designing and connecting real databases of their own.
program_overview.description:
Behind Instagram, Spotify and every game leaderboard sits the same quiet skill: SQL, the language of data. This live online course teaches it properly to students aged 13 to 18, from the first SELECT to real database design, in five honest months. SQL is one of the highest-value skills per hour of learning in all of computing: the language is compact, the concepts are learnable at 13, and the skill stays current for decades.

The arc is practical from the first week: students query and build real databases about things they care about, music libraries, game inventories, school clubs, then learn the query toolkit (functions, aggregation, subqueries), real design (relationships, joins, ER diagrams, constraints), the power features professionals lean on (views, stored procedures, transactions, indexes), and finish by securing a database and connecting it to Python, where data becomes an actual application. The capstone is a complete, well-designed, connected database project defended at demo day.

The pace is honest: five months at two live classes a week plus two to three hours of practice, with a sixth month in hand for students who need more time. Homework after every class, monthly mixed reviews that reach back deliberately, and a final exam that decides the certificate, with a free retest after revision. Real queries, real design, depth over dopamine.
what_makes_this_different: Honest length: SQL fundamentals to real design in 5 months, not a stretched year
Teen-real datasets: music, games, clubs and leaderboards, not employee-salary tables from 1998
Design is taught, not skipped: ER diagrams, normalization and constraints, the part that separates users from designers
The professional features that matter: views, procedures, transactions and indexes, each earning its place
Ends connected: MySQL driven from Python, so the database becomes an application
Real assessment: weekly homework, monthly mixed reviews, and a final exam that decides the certificate, with focused revision and a free retest

career_outcomes: A portfolio of designed, documented databases crowned by a Python-connected capstone
The data literacy every later path assumes: web development, data science, app development
A skill scholarships of time: SQL learned at 15 is still current at 40
Natural next steps: our Python, data science or full-stack courses, entered with the data layer already owned

month_3.title: Month 3: Real Database Design

week_9.title: Table Relationships and JOINS

faqs.question: Why should a teenager learn SQL and MySQL?
faqs.answer: Because it is the highest-value-per-hour skill in computing: a compact language, learnable at 13, running underneath every app they use, and still current decades from now. SQL turns a teen from someone who uses apps into someone who understands how apps remember, and it quietly powers every later path: web development, data science, app building and analytics.

faqs.question: How long does it take a teen to learn MySQL properly?
faqs.answer: Five months at 2 live classes a week plus 2 to 3 hours of practice: foundations, the query toolkit, real database design, professional features, and a Python-connected capstone. The course keeps a sixth month in hand for students who need more repetition, no rushing and no penalty. First real queries run in class one.

faqs.question: How is my teen assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No. Homework follows every class, each month ends with a mixed assignment that deliberately revisits earlier topics, and the course ends with a final exam: a practical database build plus written questions from the whole syllabus. Passing earns the certificate; falling short earns focused revision and a free retest.

faqs.question: What will my teen actually build?
faqs.answer: A dozen real databases: music libraries, game inventories and club registers in the early months, then a properly designed multi-table schema with an ER diagram, and finally the capstone, a secured, documented database connected to a small Python interface, presented at demo day. Real data about things they care about, from week one.

faqs.question: Does this course cover connecting databases to apps and websites?
faqs.answer: Yes, that is the destination: month 5 drives MySQL from Python, turning the database into an application, and the capstone requires it. Students heading to our full-stack or app development courses arrive with the data layer, usually the hardest part for beginners, already owned.

faqs.question: Is any paid software required?
faqs.answer: No. MySQL Community Server, MySQL Workbench and Python are all free, and a standard computer runs everything comfortably. SQL is famously light on hardware.

faqs.question: Is there a free trial class?

faqs.question: Are classes live or recorded?
faqs.answer: Live, always: small interactive groups with a real instructor, never pre-recorded videos. SQL is learned by writing queries and being corrected in the moment, a video cannot see your WHERE clause.
